title: Root-finder failure gives a bad empty-set decision
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f$ be a Boolean function on sign vectors of length $n$ that is not constant. Let an outcome be either absent or a decision for the restriction with no fixed coordinates. If the root-finder outcome is bad—meaning it is absent, is a constant decision, or, when it selects a coordinate, that coordinate has zero influence on $f$—then the outcome is bad as a decision for the empty-set restriction with the fixed assignment taking value $1$ wherever required.
hypotheses_covered: the target is a Boolean function on sign vectors of length $n$
the outcome is an optional decision for the empty-set restriction
the root-finder outcome satisfies its badness condition
